title: Converge client library dependencies and prune legacy API surface
creator: Aisha Park
description:
Summary: Reduce long-term maintenance and runtime variance by aligning Python/JS/Go clients onto a converged dependency set, removing deprecated API surface (legacy response wrappers and old transport params), and performing lightweight refactors that unlock performance-sensitive bundling/packing. Goals: 1) Unify common transitive deps to a single supported major where possible (http clients, retry libs, proto/runtime helpers). 2) Remove / deprecate legacy API shims that are rarely used but complicate type surfaces and polyfills. 3) Run targeted benchmarks to ensure median latency regression <= 5% and p95 unchanged or improved after changes. 4) Provide clear migration guides and automated codemods for customers and internal repos.

Scope: - Python (redwood-python): bump requests/httpx adapters, drop legacy response wrapper shims, update packaging to avoid duplicate transitive deps. - JavaScript/TypeScript (redwood-js): align fetch/transport adapters, consolidate polyfills, prune old params that were obsoleted by the transport abstraction. - Go (redwood-go): update net/http wrappers, remove deprecated client constructors, ensure go.mod replaces avoid version conflicts.

Plan and milestones: - Phase 0 (Design & Inventory, 1 week): audit current transitive graph across released client versions, identify divergence points and largest conflicting deps. - Phase 1 (Refactor & Small API removals, 2 weeks): introduce internal compatibility layer for transports; land minimal breaking changes behind feature flags; add deprecation warnings in runtime logs. - Phase 2 (Dependency bumps, 1 week): bump target dependencies in each client, update lockfiles, run full test matrices. - Phase 3 (Bench & Canary, 1 week): run perf harness (end-to-end and unit token-level), roll canaries to internal services and dedicated staging; collect telemetry. - Phase 4 (Docs & Migration, 1 week): publish migration guides, codemods, and release notes. - Phase 5 (Cleanup & Removal, after 30-day deprecation window): remove deprecated surface from v-next major and publish breaking-change migration guide.

Acceptance criteria: - All three client libraries build clean with unified dependency constraint set and no duplicate heavy transitive libs. - CI test matrix (linux/windows/mac, python 3.9-3.11, node 16-20, go 1.20-1.22) green. - Benchmarks show median token latency <= 5% regression (or improved) and p95 not worse than current baseline. - Clear migration docs + at least one automated codemod per language. - No open blocker regressions in canary windows.

Risks & mitigations: - Breaking changes to public API: mitigate with feature flags, deprecation warnings, and codemods. - Unexpected transitive breakages for large customers: coordinate with customer success for affected accounts and offer patch branches. - Performance regressions in edge cases: keep the ability to pin older client version per route in Console routing during rollout.
comments: 2026-03-02 — Inventory completed: found 3 major divergence points between clients: retry libs, backoff helpers, and the legacy response wrapper. See spreadsheet: https://drive.redwood/company/client-dep-inventory-2026

2026-03-04 — Design review with SDK leads. Decided to implement a thin transport adapter to reduce surface churn and enable bumping fetch/httpx without breaking callers. Action: ENG-42490 assigned to prototype adapter in redwood-js.
2026-03-06 — Prototype PR for transport adapter (redwood-js): https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-js/pull/1423 — early benchmarks show 3% median improvement when deduping polyfills.

2026-03-08 — Python change landed behind flag: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-python/pull/978 — note: one downstream internal repo required a patch to handle new response typing; outreach sent to owners.
2026-03-10 — CI matrix failure on node 20 caused by a transitive dependency change; reverted bump and added a constraint in package.json. Resolved by updating dev tooling in ENG-42511.

2026-03-11 — Canary rollout to internal staging (10% of routes) started. Telemetry dashboard: https://console.redwood/observability/clients/eng-42488 — initial p95 unchanged, token cost decreased ~2% on JS SDK paths.

2026-03-12 — Blocker: one enterprise customer reported TS compile errors due to stricter types after removing legacy overloads. Decision: reintroduce a compatibility overload shim in a patch release and extend customer outreach before final removal.
